1.title: System Call Commands in Linux

2.title: Process Related Commands in Linux
2.answer:
Important process-related commands:

top    - displays running processes and resource usage.
ps     - displays process information.
kill   - sends a signal to a process.
wait   - waits for a child process to finish (shell built-in / system-call concept).
sleep  - pauses execution for a specified time.
nice   - starts a process with a specified CPU scheduling priority.
renice - changes the priority of an existing process.
bg     - resumes a stopped job in the background.
fg     - brings a background/stopped job to the foreground.

Examples:
top
ps
ps aux
kill PID
sleep 5
nice -n 10 command
renice 10 -p PID
jobs
bg
fg

3.title: Messages to Logged-in Users and Shared Memory
3.answer:
3(a) Commands for sending messages to logged-in users:

who    - shows users currently logged in.
cat    - displays the contents of a file; it can be used with a terminal device for messaging.
wall   - broadcasts a message to all logged-in users.
write  - sends a message to a specific logged-in user.
mesg   - controls whether other users can write messages to your terminal.

Examples:
who
wall "System maintenance in 5 minutes"
write username
mesg y
mesg n

3(b) List processes and IPC objects associated with System V IPC:

ipcs        - displays IPC facilities.
ipcs -m     - displays shared-memory segments.
ipcs -q     - displays message queues.
ipcs -s     - displays semaphore arrays.

Example:
ipcs -m

4.title: FCFS CPU Scheduling
4.answer:
Python program to calculate average waiting time and average turnaround time using First Come First Serve (FCFS).

Formula:
Waiting Time = Completion Time - Arrival Time - Burst Time
Turnaround Time = Completion Time - Arrival Time

Program:
4.code:
n = int(input("Enter number of processes: "))
bt = []
for i in range(n):
    bt.append(int(input(f"Enter burst time for P{i+1}: ")))

wt = [0] * n
tat = [0] * n

for i in range(1, n):
    wt[i] = wt[i-1] + bt[i-1]

for i in range(n):
    tat[i] = wt[i] + bt[i]

print("\nProcess\tBurst\tWaiting\tTurnaround")
for i in range(n):
    print(f"P{i+1}\t{bt[i]}\t{wt[i]}\t{tat[i]}")

print(f"\nAverage Waiting Time: {sum(wt)/n:.2f}")
print(f"Average Turnaround Time: {sum(tat)/n:.2f}")

5.title: SJF CPU Scheduling
5.answer:
Python program to calculate average waiting time and average turnaround time using non-preemptive Shortest Job First (SJF).

The processes are arranged in ascending order of burst time.
5.code:
n = int(input("Enter number of processes: "))
processes = []

for i in range(n):
    bt = int(input(f"Enter burst time for P{i+1}: "))
    processes.append([i + 1, bt])

processes.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])

wt = [0] * n
tat = [0] * n

for i in range(1, n):
    wt[i] = wt[i-1] + processes[i-1][1]

for i in range(n):
    tat[i] = wt[i] + processes[i][1]

print("\nProcess\tBurst\tWaiting\tTurnaround")
for i in range(n):
    print(f"P{processes[i][0]}\t{processes[i][1]}\t{wt[i]}\t{tat[i]}")

print(f"\nAverage Waiting Time: {sum(wt)/n:.2f}")
print(f"Average Turnaround Time: {sum(tat)/n:.2f}")

6.title: Priority CPU Scheduling
6.answer:
Python program for non-preemptive Priority CPU Scheduling.

Lower numerical value is treated as higher priority.
6.code:
n = int(input("Enter number of processes: "))
processes = []

for i in range(n):
    bt = int(input(f"Enter burst time for P{i+1}: "))
    priority = int(input(f"Enter priority for P{i+1}: "))
    processes.append([i + 1, bt, priority])

processes.sort(key=lambda x: x[2])

wt = [0] * n
tat = [0] * n

for i in range(1, n):
    wt[i] = wt[i-1] + processes[i-1][1]

for i in range(n):
    tat[i] = wt[i] + processes[i][1]

print("\nProcess\tBurst\tPriority\tWaiting\tTurnaround")
for i, p in enumerate(processes):
    print(f"P{p[0]}\t{p[1]}\t{p[2]}\t\t{wt[i]}\t{tat[i]}")

print(f"\nAverage Waiting Time: {sum(wt)/n:.2f}")
print(f"Average Turnaround Time: {sum(tat)/n:.2f}")

7.title: Round Robin CPU Scheduling
7.answer: Python program to calculate average waiting time and average turnaround time using Round Robin CPU Scheduling.
7.code:
n = int(input("Enter number of processes: "))
bt = []

for i in range(n):
    bt.append(int(input(f"Enter burst time for P{i+1}: ")))

quantum = int(input("Enter time quantum: "))

remaining = bt.copy()
wt = [0] * n
tat = [0] * n
time = 0

while any(r > 0 for r in remaining):
    for i in range(n):
        if remaining[i] > 0:
            execution = min(quantum, remaining[i])
            time += execution
            remaining[i] -= execution

            if remaining[i] == 0:
                tat[i] = time
                wt[i] = tat[i] - bt[i]

print("\nProcess\tBurst\tWaiting\tTurnaround")
for i in range(n):
    print(f"P{i+1}\t{bt[i]}\t{wt[i]}\t{tat[i]}")

print(f"\nAverage Waiting Time: {sum(wt)/n:.2f}")
print(f"Average Turnaround Time: {sum(tat)/n:.2f}")

8.title: Banker's Algorithm
8.answer:
Python program to implement the Banker's Algorithm for deadlock avoidance.

The program calculates the Need matrix and checks whether the system is in a safe state.
8.code:
n = int(input("Enter number of processes: "))
m = int(input("Enter number of resource types: "))

print("Enter Allocation matrix:")
allocation = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

print("Enter Max matrix:")
maximum = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

print("Enter Available resources:")
available = list(map(int, input().split()))

need = [[maximum[i][j] - allocation[i][j] for j in range(m)]
        for i in range(n)]

work = available.copy()
finish = [False] * n
safe_sequence = []

while len(safe_sequence) < n:
    found = False

    for i in range(n):
        if not finish[i] and all(need[i][j] <= work[j] for j in range(m)):
            for j in range(m):
                work[j] += allocation[i][j]
            finish[i] = True
            safe_sequence.append(i)
            found = True

    if not found:
        break

print("\nNeed Matrix:")
for row in need:
    print(*row)

if len(safe_sequence) == n:
    print("\nSystem is in a SAFE state.")
    print("Safe sequence:", " -> ".join(f"P{i}" for i in safe_sequence))
else:
    print("\nSystem is NOT in a safe state.")

10.title: FIFO Page Replacement
10.answer:
Python program to implement First In First Out (FIFO) Page Replacement.

FIFO replaces the page that has been in memory for the longest time.
10.code:
pages = list(map(int, input("Enter reference string: ").split()))
frames = int(input("Enter number of frames: "))

memory = []
faults = 0

print("\nPage\tFrames\t\tStatus")

for page in pages:
    if page not in memory:
        faults += 1
        if len(memory) < frames:
            memory.append(page)
        else:
            memory.pop(0)
            memory.append(page)
        status = "Page Fault"
    else:
        status = "Hit"

    print(f"{page}\t{memory}\t{status}")

print(f"\nTotal Page Faults: {faults}")
print(f"Total Page Hits: {len(pages) - faults}")

11.title: LRU Page Replacement
11.answer:
Python program to implement Least Recently Used (LRU) Page Replacement.

LRU replaces the page that has not been used for the longest time.
11.code:
pages = list(map(int, input("Enter reference string: ").split()))
frames = int(input("Enter number of frames: "))

memory = []
faults = 0

print("\nPage\tFrames\t\tStatus")

for page in pages:
    if page in memory:
        memory.remove(page)
        memory.append(page)
        status = "Hit"
    else:
        faults += 1
        if len(memory) >= frames:
            memory.pop(0)
        memory.append(page)
        status = "Page Fault"

    print(f"{page}\t{memory}\t{status}")

print(f"\nTotal Page Faults: {faults}")
print(f"Total Page Hits: {len(pages) - faults}")
